title: Sandbars, drinking rules and crew accidents
summary: Waiting on sandbars, sneaking drinks, and a deckhand killed in Davenport.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: What's the longest you got stuck on a sandbar?

Oh, I mean, well, they had to figure out that thing to work with. I mean, I remember, because I mean, we'd be praying, and we'd get tired, you know what I mean? You get tired, but you got to pray. Be getting people happy. And I remember sometime, before the war, you remember, I know you wouldn't remember about that, during the robbery, you probably would, but before, I'm going to say I went into the war, and I went into the war, there were people committing suicide. That was, we would jump off that bull.

Yeah. But it was a happy thing, and people would enjoy themselves. Now, there was women, men would sneak alcohol on us. They sold root beer. They didn't sell no alcohol, but they sold beer, I think. They sold beer. I know strong, but women would sneak as ever. Men would sneak their bottles. We did the same thing. We'd sneak our bottles. But don't let them catch you drunk. Don't let them get the musician on that stand drunk while he can't do his job. And then there was help. From the deckhand to the porter and the cashiers and everything. Don't mess with them. I mean, you had to be on the lake. And this man, this black man, and this woman, I know they weren't in the race or nothing, but, and this other black guy I told you about, that was his daddy, my son, I got to believe his daddy. He was the head man for the deckhand. He controlled them. Sometimes they had white deckhand, they didn't want to listen to him, but he'd go. He'd let them all. But that man had experience, he knew what to do. And I say a captain has a whole lot of responsibility on his end, but he had a lot of assistance. He'd always have about six guys, white guys, and one black guy worked for him a long time. He did everything. And he could trust them, he knew them. He had one guy got killed in Davenport. He'd be waiting for the cup of the slalom, nobody would look and see how it happened. But he went out that Saturday night and got drunk. And they had two of them, a sternum on each side. Not a sternum, but the thing that pushed his sternum back there. And he went to come in and get soap off as possible, and this thing had stopped. And before this engineer does that, he rings the bell. He didn't hear that bell. He had this thing down in there. Before we get to this thing that's going this way, it's one thing going this way, then it's very very good thing going this way.
And he had his head down in there and the man pushed that button.

And nobody can understand, because that man has been working with him for so many years. So yeah, I actually think it can happen if the person knows the danger of certain things. You see? And another guy, he's from Spain, and he and I used to talk a lot, because he always had a little fishing place. You could fish if you want. He loved eel. He and I used to talk, that's in a time when Spain was having trouble among the government. Well, I used to talk to him about the situation, how that happened. And that's why he left Spain, because I think it was a comic or something that was trying to take over Spain, which they did in a while, I think. This is about in the 30s, them talking about. They had a big war.
